Identity: Executive Order 10978, Establishing Presidential Awards for Significant Contributions to the Export Expansion Program, signed by John F. Kennedy at the White House on December 5, 1961, F.R. Doc. 61-11651 filed Dec. 6, 1961, at 26 FR 11714 (FR of 1961-12-07); this agrees with the OFR catalog row. Inventory: sections 1, 2, 3, 3(a), 3(b), 4, 5 and 6 are all the operative text. The preamble is recital only. Ending: the order has no own-terms end. The 1989 OFR codification prints it with no amendment or revocation note. The OFR catalog record has no disposition note. The current-law job has no U.S. Code or eCFR mention. The number search of the held corpus finds only the order, the 1989 codification and the 2011 Commerce notice, and that notice says the E Award Program was established by EO 10978 and describes the Secretary of Commerce procedures (application form ITA-725P), so the program was still running in 2011. No held source records an amendment, revocation, supersession or statutory repeal. Current predicate: the claim openly rests on the original text plus bounded searches through the cutoff and calls this absence-of-ending evidence, not a positive 2026 source. That description is accurate, and for an unrevoked standing order with no own-terms end it supports operative status at 2026-10-14. Savings: none needed. Search descriptions match the machine search records (0/0/0 hits). Minor, non-material: the section 6 judgment says 'lapel pin' where the text says 'a suitably designed pin'. This is a paraphrase, not a quotation, and does not affect the result.

defects.source_says: Sec. 6 of the held text reads 'This Order shall be effective on April 1, 1978.' (signed March 27, 1978). The revocation of EO 11312 took effect on 1978-04-01, and the claim's own judgment_reason and research_rationale say 1978-04-01. The date cannot precede the order's signing.
defects.problem: Wrong first-end date, inconsistent with the cited source and with the claim itself.

defects.source_says: Sec. 6: 'This Order shall be effective on April 1, 1978.' The judgment_reason itself says the provision was exhausted on 1978-04-01.

defects.claim_says: the International Communication Agency, renamed the United States Information Agency by EO 12388
defects.source_says: The EO 12388 preamble (47 FR 46245) says Section 303 of Public Law 97-241 'changed the name of the International Communication Agency back to its original name of the United States Information Agency'. EO 12388 only conformed EO 12047 to the change.
defects.problem: Wrong actor for the renaming: it was a statute, not the order.

defects.claim_says: only EO 12388 is listed. The judgment calls the Department of State's present role 'a substitution of officer, not an end' without giving the date, actor, mechanism or source.
defects.source_says: The held U.S. Code note printing EO 12047 at 22 U.S.C. 2459 (release point 119-121) adds: '[For abolition of United States Information Agency ..., transfer of functions, and treatment of references thereto, see sections 6531, 6532, and 6551 of this title.]'. The 2026-10-02 notice also relies on the Foreign Affairs Reform and Restructuring Act of 1998.
defects.problem: A statutory later event (the abolition of USIA and the transfer of the designated officer's functions to the Secretary of State) is not recorded as a later_event with an effective date, actor, mechanism and source. The rationale says the U.S. Code note records no revocation but does not mention its abolition and transfer cross-reference.

Identity: Executive Order 12047, Imported Objects of Cultural Significance, of March 27, 1978 (Carter), 43 FR 13359, F.R. Doc. 78-8495 filed 3-28-78; this agrees with the catalog. The six-clause inventory is complete. The outcome is plausible. Sections 1-3 and 5 are still relied on: the Department of State's notice of 2026-10-02 cites EO 12047, and EO 12388 only substituted the agency name, effective as of 1982-08-24. Sections 4 and 6 were performed when the order took effect. But the first_end dates of sections 4 and 6 are both given as 1975-04-01. That is a date before the order was signed, and it contradicts section 6 ('effective on April 1, 1978') and the claim's own reasons, which say 1978-04-01. A wrong exact date on a terminated clause is disqualifying. In addition, the claim credits the 1982 renaming to EO 12388 when the held text attributes it to Pub. L. 97-241 sec. 303. It also leaves the statutory abolition of USIA and the transfer of its functions to the Secretary of State, flagged in the held U.S. Code note, unrecorded as a later event.

Later orders: I read the held texts of EO 11249 (6.01-3, 6.01-4, new 6.01-5, 6.04-5, new 6.04-6, 6.04-7), EO 13143 (6.01-4), EO 13273 (new 6.01-6, 6.04-1) and EO 14116 (6.01-3 through 6.19-1, including 6.10-7 but not 6.10-1). Identity: Executive Order 12403, African Development Bank, of February 8, 1983, 48 FR 6087 (FR of 1983-02-10), F.R. Doc. 83-3864. The signature is lost in the OCR, but the catalog row gives Reagan. Inventory: sections 1-3 are all the operative text. Sec. 1: the current U.S. Code 22 U.S.C. 288 note and 8 CFR 316.20 (GovInfo bulk copy dated 2026-11-05) still list the African Development Bank under E.O. 12403, and nothing held amends it. Sec. 2: EO 12567, 12647 and 12766 each struck and re-inserted the end of the lists in EO 11269 sections 2(c), 3(d) and 7, keeping the Bank. EO 13118 sec. 10(9) changed only 1(b), 4(a) and section 7's heading and opening words, effective April 1, 1999 under sec. 11. All of this I verified in the held texts, and the before-and-after is recorded as the strike-and-insert ruling requires. The current 22 U.S.C. 286b note prints EO 11269 with the Bank in all three places and lists EO 12403 in its status line, with nothing after EO 13118. Sec. 3: the release point 119-121 carries delegation notes under 290i-1(c), 290i-2, 290i-6(a) and 290i-9(b) citing EO 12403. No own-terms end, savings issue or missed later event was found. The OFR catalog search has no note naming EO 12403 as affected; its own record notes only 'Amends: EO 11269', which the claim covers.
